- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently underestimates true mean in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply slight upward bias (1–3%) to mean forecast.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price correction), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day true value.  
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model often overreacts; dampen forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
